metric.why: Distributed AI training is unusually intolerant of network degradation; a lossy fabric shows up as wasted GPU-hours before it shows up as an outage.
metric.metric: Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth
metric.definition: Continuous measurement of round-trip latency, loss rate, and utilization on the facility's internal fabric and external transit.

reading.body:
Network latency, packet loss, and bandwidth sit in the same uptime category as backup power, because a lossy fabric burns GPU-hours before it causes an outage.

The metric is filed under uptime and redundancy, alongside UPS battery health and generator runtime and SLA uptime compliance. That grouping is the point. The internal fabric is treated as a continuity asset rather than a performance nicety, and it is measured continuously on round-trip latency, loss rate, and utilization across both the facility's internal fabric and its external transit.

For AI specifically, the failure mode differs from a power failure. A generator that does not start is binary and visible. Network degradation is partial, and distributed training is unusually intolerant of it, so the cost appears first as wasted GPU-hours rather than as downtime. That makes this a leading indicator rather than a lagging one, which is why it belongs next to the power metrics instead of in a separate performance bucket.

What the data does not contain is any measured value. There are no thresholds, no targets, no latency or loss figures, no facility names, and no time series. It defines what to measure and where, not what any network currently reads. The sibling list also shows only two other uptime metrics, so this is a partial view of how the category is populated, not a complete inventory.

siblings.label: UPS battery health and generator runtime
